item.title: Southeast Asia turns to nuclear power to fuel AI data center boom
item.description:
Several Southeast Asian nations are resurrecting long-shelved nuclear energy programs as the region races to meet surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence data centers, with the ongoing war in Iran adding urgency by disrupting global energy supplies and driving up fossil fuel costs.

Five of the ten members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations — Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and the Philippines — are now actively pursuing nuclear power, with nearly half the region potentially incorporating nuclear energy by the 2030s, according to the Associated Press. The push coincides with a broader global movement in which nearly 40 countries have pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050.

item.title: Iran quietly reviews US ceasefire plan despite public rejection
item.description: Iran is still reviewing a 15-point American proposal to end the war in the Persian Gulf despite publicly dismissing it, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday, as oil prices rebounded from earlier losses and gold climbed on persistent uncertainty over the conflict's trajectory.

item.title: Rice researchers recover 95% of battery metals using plasma and citric acid
item.description: Researchers at Rice University have developed a new method for recycling lithium-ion batteries that recovers nearly 95 percent of valuable metals using microwave-induced plasma and citric acid — the same acid found in lemons. The patented process, published in the journal Advanced Materials, offers a lower-energy, less chemically intensive alternative to current industrial recycling techniques.

item.title: Gold slides, oil holds above $100 as Iran rejects U.S. ceasefire plan
item.description: Gold fell below $4,500 per ounce on Thursday morning while oil prices remained elevated above $100 a barrel as markets digested the collapse of a U.S. ceasefire proposal to Iran and the ongoing military conflict across the Middle East.

item.title: IBM says quantum computer matched lab data in materials simulation
item.description: IBM announced on Thursday that its quantum computer has accurately simulated the behavior of a real magnetic material, producing results that match neutron scattering experiments conducted at national laboratories. The achievement, which researchers say was previously considered beyond the reach of current quantum hardware, marks a turning point in the effort to use quantum computers as practical tools for scientific discovery.

item.title: Dollar slips in Asia as Iran diplomacy doubts dim Fed hike bets
item.description:
The U.S. dollar edged lower in Asian trading on Thursday as investors sought clarity on whether diplomatic efforts could bring a de-escalation in the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran, while scaling back expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate hikes later this year.

The U.S. dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, slipped 0.1% after posting its largest one-day gain in a week during the prior session. The dollar remained near 99.5, below the ten-month highs reached earlier in March when the conflict first sent energy prices surging.

item.title: Israel strikes Isfahan as Iran fires missiles at Tel Aviv
item.description:
Israel launched a series of strikes on Iranian military and nuclear facilities around Isfahan on Thursday, as Iran retaliated with two missile barrages targeting central Israel, marking another day of escalation in a nearly month-long war even as President Donald Trump insists Tehran is ready to negotiate.

The Israel Defense Forces said they had completed strikes on what they called critical infrastructure in Isfahan, a city that hosts a major air base and nuclear sites previously targeted during the conflict. Iran responded with missile volleys that activated air raid sirens in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, with rescue teams dispatched to impact sites in central Israel. An Israeli soldier was also killed by rocket fire from Lebanon, where Hezbollah has been launching attacks since early March.

item.title: OECD warns U.S. inflation could hit 4.2% amid Iran war oil shock
item.description: The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development warned Thursday that US headline inflation could reach 4.2% in 2026, sharply higher than its previous estimate of 3%, as the ongoing US-Israel military conflict with Iran sends global energy prices soaring. The revised projection, published in the OECD's interim economic outlook, is more than double the Federal Reserve's 2% target and marks one of the steepest upward revisions the organization has made in a single quarter.

item.title: IRGC Navy chief killed in Israeli strike on Bandar Abbas
item.description:
Israel killed the commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy, Alireza Tangsiri, in a strike on the southern Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas, an Israeli official told The Jerusalem Post on Thursday. The killing of Tangsiri, who oversaw Iranian naval operations near the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints, marks a further escalation in the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28. Iranian authorities had not publicly confirmed the killing as of Thursday morning.

The strike came as Iranian ballistic missiles continued to target Israel, with sirens sounding across central Israel on Thursday morning. The IDF said it detected and intercepted an Iranian missile launch targeting central Israel, while six people were lightly wounded across two separate barrages earlier in the day. An 11-year-old girl in Safed suffered cardiac arrest during an air-raid siren and was hospitalized in serious condition.

item.title: Trump pushes aides to end Iran war within weeks
item.description: President Trump has privately told associates in recent days that he wants to avoid a protracted war in Iran and hopes to bring the conflict to a close in the coming weeks, according to the Wall Street Journal. Nearly a month into Operation Epic Fury, which began on February 28, Trump has informed advisers he believes the conflict is in its final stages and has urged them to stick to the four-to-six-week timeline he has publicly outlined.

item.title: Iran formalizes Strait of Hormuz toll as US troops head to region
item.description: Iran has begun operating the Strait of Hormuz as a "de facto toll booth," demanding transit fees from commercial vessels while selectively blocking ships linked to the United States and Israel, according to an analysis published Thursday by Lloyd's List Intelligence. The practice has drawn sharp condemnation from Gulf Arab states and comes as thousands of American troops move toward the region, giving President Donald Trump options for potential military action against Iran.

item.title: UK authorizes military to board Russian shadow fleet tankers
item.description:
A naval drone struck a sanctioned oil tanker laden with Russian crude near the Bosporus Strait early Thursday, just as northern European leaders meeting in Helsinki pledged to crack down harder on Russia's "shadow fleet" of sanctions-evading vessels.

The Sierra Leone-flagged tanker Altura, carrying about 140,000 tonnes of crude oil from the Russian port of Novorossiysk, sustained damage to its bridge and engine room roughly 14 nautical miles north of the Bosporus, according to the Associated Press. All 27 Turkish crew members were unharmed. Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu described the incident as "an attack by an unmanned sea vessel" but did not attribute blame. No party has claimed responsibility, though Ukraine has previously used sea drones against Russian-linked shipping in the Black Sea.

The Altura, owned by Turkey-based Pergamon Maritime since November 2025, has been subject to European Union sanctions since October for its role in transporting Russian oil exports, according to the Open Sanctions database.

item.title: Iran-backed FPV drones hit US helicopter, radar at Baghdad base
item.description: Iran-backed Iraqi militias have struck a U.S. Black Hawk helicopter and a key air-defense radar at Camp Victory in Baghdad using fiber-optic-guided first-person-view drones, marking a sharp escalation in the type of weaponry being turned against American forces in the Middle East. The attacks, footage of which circulated online this week, mirror tactics refined on the battlefields of Ukraine — and arrive just as Ukrainian drone commanders descended on Washington to warn that the United States now faces the same cheap-drone saturation problem they have been fighting since 2022.

item.title: Trump says Iran let 10 oil tankers through Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
President Donald Trump disclosed on Thursday that Iran permitted 10 oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz, revealing what he had cryptically described earlier this week as a "very big present" from Tehran linked to the ongoing conflict.

Speaking at a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Trump said Iranian interlocutors had offered the gesture to demonstrate their seriousness about potential negotiations to end the nearly month-long war. "They said, to show you the fact that we're real and solid and we're there, we're going to let you have eight boats of oil, eight boats, eight big boats of oil," Trump said, according to Reuters. "I guess they were right, and they were real, and I think they were Pakistani-flagged... It ended up being 10 boats."

item.title: Researchers encode data using three light properties in holographic storage first
item.description: Researchers at Fujian Normal University in China have developed a holographic data storage system that encodes information using three properties of light simultaneously — amplitude, phase, and polarization — a method they say can pack more data into a single holographic page and simplify readout using artificial intelligence.

item.title: Apple plans to open Siri to rival AI chatbots in iOS 27
item.description: Apple is planning to open Siri to rival artificial intelligence services, ending OpenAI's exclusive chatbot partnership with the iPhone maker and transforming the device into a broader AI platform, Bloomberg reported on Thursday. The move will allow companies like Google and Anthropic to integrate their chatbots directly with Siri in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.

item.title: Fossil ape found in Egypt challenges East Africa origin theory
item.description:
A newly identified fossil ape unearthed in northern Egypt is prompting scientists to reconsider where modern apes — including humans — first evolved. The species, named Masripithecus moghraensis, lived roughly 17 to 18 million years ago and represents the first definitive fossil ape ever found in North Africa, according to a study published Thursday in the journal Science.

An international team from Egypt's Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center and the University of Southern California recovered the fossils — a partial lower jaw and several teeth — from the Wadi Moghra site in northern Egypt during fieldwork in 2023 and 2024.

item.title: Study finds AI chatbots affirm users 49% more than humans do
item.description: A new study published Thursday in the journal Science found that leading AI chatbots are so prone to flattering their users that they routinely dispense bad advice, damage relationships, and reinforce harmful behaviors. The research, led by Stanford University scientists, tested 11 major AI systems and found they all exhibited varying degrees of sycophancy — overly agreeable behavior that users, paradoxically, tend to prefer.

item.title: Trump extends pause on Iran energy strikes to April 6
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Thursday announced he would extend a halt on U.S. military strikes targeting Iran's energy infrastructure by 10 days, pushing the deadline to April 6 as the White House signaled both diplomatic openness and a readiness to escalate.

"As per Iranian Government request I am pausing the period of Energy Plant destruction by 10 Days to Monday, April 6, 2026, at 8 P.M., Eastern Time," Trump wrote on Truth Social, according to CNBC. He added that "talks are ongoing and they are going very well," pushing back against what he called "erroneous statements" from the media.

item.title: US senators introduce bill to sanction Hungary over Ukraine aid blockade
item.description:
A bipartisan group of US senators has introduced legislation that would impose financial sanctions and visa bans on Hungarian government officials, escalating Washington's response to Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's continued obstruction of a €90 billion European Union loan to Ukraine. The bill, called the Block Putin Act, was put forward by Senators Jeanne Shaheen, a Democrat from New Hampshire, and Thom Tillis, a Republican from North Carolina, according to the Financial Times.

The move comes as Orbán, facing his toughest re-election fight in 16 years ahead of April 12 parliamentary elections, has deepened an anti-Ukraine campaign that now includes allegations of Ukrainian intelligence interference in Hungarian domestic politics.
